_notes: Iron Man, code 1.86, the non-Vault ROM (im_186). Measured on a 286-sample live recording on the 4KP
(2026-09-15): a volume nudge in the operator menu, coins, one three-ball game with a mid-ball tilt
on ball 1, attract.
NVRAM side is identical to im_186ve: scores at 0x021109E4 stride 4, credits 0x0211100C, volume
0x02110248 with complement, the '+2 family' adjustment records (free play 35, balls 32, max credits
34) with their check bytes, and the five high-score / eight mode-champion records from 0x02102C18
and 0x02102CB8 (32-byte records, checksum16 at +28), all validating on the captured image.
The CPU side differs from both Vault ROMs: the ball is at 0x00037715 (1, 2, 3 through the game,
parked afterwards), the player at 0x00037714, and the status bitfield at ball+0x31 = 0x00037746
with the usual 1 in attract, 20 in play, 22 while tilted -- game_over is mask 0x14 inverted and
tilted bit 0x02, the tilt covering exactly the samples from the tilt to the end of ball 1 with
player 1's score frozen. On im_186 the 1.86VE addresses 0x34DB9/0x34DB8/0x34DEA read 0, 2 and 0
throughout, which is why the two 1.86 ROMs carry separate maps.
Mode champion labels are the attract order (Bogey, Iron Man, War Machine, Iron Monger, Whiplash,
Drones, Jericho, Do Or Die Multiball); the record order matches the default-threshold table.

Names are declared 11 bytes null-terminated: with Standard Adjustment #36 set to 10 LETTER NAME and the high scores reset, this ROM wrote factory names of up to nine characters (ROTHARMEL, BANGERJAY) into the records, verified on a saved image.
2026-11: tilted is the value 0x16 (mask 0x1F) on 0x00037746: bit 0x02 is set in 72, a mode value
a headless game read.
2026-11: The A.1 (64) and A.2 (52) adjustments added from the ROM image (README, 'Adjustments
from the ROM').
Confirmed on a cabinet 2026-11-13 (ALP4K; two players, tilt on P1 ball 1): 1,008,280 /
1,659,970, the records and the status byte (01, 14 play, 16 tilted) matched the DMD.
